stem:
Meena fills two identical steel bowls, each half full. One bowl has uncooked rice and the other has cotton wool. The bowl with rice feels much heavier than the bowl with cotton wool.

What can Meena correctly conclude?

options.text: Both bowls have the same mass because they are identical bowls filled to the same level.
The bowl of rice has more mass because rice is the heavier material.
The bowl of cotton wool has more mass because cotton wool is fluffier and takes up more space.
The masses cannot be compared because rice and cotton wool are different materials.

teacher.key_rationale: Heaviness comparison is a relative mass comparison: the heavier-feeling bowl (rice) has more mass. Option A is the trap for a student who treats identical containers filled to the same level as having the same mass; C swaps volume/fluffiness for mass; D wrongly claims comparison is impossible.
